title: Coefficient section with prescribed p-basis lifts
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero complete Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] of characteristic $p>0$, with residue field $k=A/\mathfrak m$. Let $(b_i)_{i\in E}$ be a $p$-basis of $k$, meaning that the finitely supported monomials $\prod_i b_i^{n_i}$, $0\leq n_i<p$, form a vector-space basis of $k$ over $k^p=\{x^p:x\in k\}$. For each $i$ choose any lift $\beta_i\in A$ of $b_i$. There is a unique field homomorphism $s:k\to A$ whose composite with the residue map is the identity and such that $s(b_i)=\beta_i$ for every $i$.

source.place: Expose IV 2.1.4, printed p.50: unique coefficient field containing arbitrary lifts of a residue-field p-basis (there attributed to Bourbaki, Algebre commutative IX, section 2, no.2, Theorem 1(a)).

proof.text: Write $q_n=p^n$ and let $D_n$ be the finitely supported exponent families $e:E\to\{0,\ldots,q_n-1\}$. Every $x\in k$ has a unique finite expansion $x=\sum_{e\in D_n}a_{n,e}(x)^{q_n}b^e$ with $a_{n,e}(x)\in k$. Here is the induction from the assumed $p$-basis, including uniqueness. At $n=0$ the only exponent is zero and its coefficient is $x$. Given the expansion at $n$, expand each $a_{n,e}(x)=\sum_f d_{e,f}^{p}b^f$ in the assumed $p$-basis. Frobenius additivity [def-weil-ring-frobenius] gives $x=\sum_{e,f}d_{e,f}^{p^{n+1}}b^{e+p^nf}$. The digit decomposition of each exponent less than $p^{n+1}$ as $e+p^nf$ is unique. Conversely, group any such expansion by $e$ and use uniqueness at level $n$, followed by uniqueness in the original $p$-basis, to recover every $d_{e,f}$. Frobenius on a field is injective: $u^{q_n}=v^{q_n}$ implies $(u-v)^{q_n}=0$, hence $u=v$. All sums are finite, even when $E$ is infinite.

source.place: Expose IV 2.1.4, printed p.50 (statement); explicit Frobenius-expansion proof supplied by Q23 since the cited Bourbaki proof is not in the literature.

proof.text: Put $R_n=A/\mathfrak m^{q_n}$, and let $\bar\beta_i$ denote the image of $\beta_i$ there. Define $t_n:k^{q_n}\to R_n$ by $t_n(a^{q_n})=\widetilde a^{q_n}\bmod\mathfrak m^{q_n}$, where $\widetilde a$ is any residue lift of $a$. The root $a$ is unique by field Frobenius injectivity. Two lifts differ by an element of $\mathfrak m$, so their $q_n$th powers differ by an element of $\mathfrak m^{q_n}$, by [def-weil-ring-frobenius]. Lifts of $a+a'$ and $aa'$ may be chosen as $\widetilde a+\widetilde {a'}$ and $\widetilde a\widetilde {a'}$; the same Frobenius identities prove that $t_n$ preserves addition, multiplication, and $1$. In particular $t_n(b_i^{q_n})=\bar\beta_i^{q_n}$.

source.place: Expose IV 2.1.4, printed p.50 (statement); explicit Frobenius-expansion proof supplied by Q23 since the cited Bourbaki proof is not in the literature.

proof.text: Using the finite expansion of Step 1, define $s_n:k\to R_n$ by $s_n(x)=\sum_e t_n(a_{n,e}(x)^{q_n})\bar\beta^e$. This is a ring homomorphism, as the following coefficient calculation shows. Addition adds the coefficients in $k^{q_n}$, so is preserved by $t_n$. For multiplication it suffices by distributivity to multiply two terms $c b^e$ and $d b^f$, with $c,d\in k^{q_n}$. Write $e_i+f_i=g_i+q_nh_i$, with $0\le g_i<q_n$. Their product in $k$ has bounded expansion $cd\prod_i(b_i^{q_n})^{h_i}b^g$. Its image is $t_n(c)t_n(d)\prod_i\bar\beta_i^{q_nh_i}\bar\beta^g=t_n(c)t_n(d)\bar\beta^{e+f}$, exactly the product of the images. The expansion of $1$ gives $s_n(1)=1$. Reducing this formula modulo $\mathfrak m$ gives $x$, so $s_n$ is a residue section. For $n\ge1$ the expansion of $b_i$ has its sole nonzero coefficient $1$ at the $i$th unit exponent, giving $s_n(b_i)=\bar\beta_i$. For $n=0$, $R_0=k$ and the same assertion is the residue-lift assumption.

source.place: Expose IV 2.1.4, printed p.50 (statement); explicit Frobenius-expansion proof supplied by Q23 since the cited Bourbaki proof is not in the literature.

proof.text:
The sections commute with $R_{n+1}\to R_n$. To check this without assuming compatibility of the chosen lifts, write the expansion of $x$ at level $n+1$ with root coefficients $d_{e,f}$ and exponent $e+q_nf$, as in Step 1. Its level-$n$ root coefficient is $a_e=\sum_f d_{e,f}^{p}b^f$. Choose arbitrary lifts $\widetilde d_{e,f}$ and $\widetilde a_e$ in $A$. The element $\widetilde a_e-\sum_f\widetilde d_{e,f}^{p}\beta^f$ lies in $\mathfrak m$ because its residue is zero. Its $q_n$th power lies in $\mathfrak m^{q_n}$, and [def-weil-ring-frobenius] therefore gives
$$\widetilde a_e^{q_n}\equiv\sum_f\widetilde d_{e,f}^{p^{n+1}}\beta^{q_nf}\pmod{\mathfrak m^{q_n}}.$$
Multiply by $\beta^e$ and sum over $e$. The left side is the formula for $s_n(x)$, and the right side is the reduction of the formula for $s_{n+1}(x)$, proving compatibility.

source.place: Expose IV 2.1.4, printed p.50 (statement); explicit Frobenius-expansion proof supplied by Q23 since the cited Bourbaki proof is not in the literature.

proof.text: For each positive integer $N$, choose $n$ with $q_n\ge N$ and reduce $s_n(x)$ to $A/\mathfrak m^N$. Compatibility in Step 4 makes this independent of $n$: two indices are compared with their maximum. These residues form a compatible tuple over all $N$. By the bijectivity of $A\to\varprojlim_N A/\mathfrak m^N$ in [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], there is a unique element $s(x)\in A$ with those residues. Addition, multiplication, and $1$ are preserved because they are preserved in every quotient and the same canonical map is injective. Thus $s:k\to A$ is a unital ring homomorphism; it is injective since its residue composite is $1_k$, so it is a field embedding into $A$. The residues of $s(b_i)$ and $\beta_i$ agree at every $N$ by Step 3; injectivity gives $s(b_i)=\beta_i$. Its residue composite is the identity by the residue-section assertion of Step 3.

source.place: Expose IV 2.1.4, printed p.50 (statement); explicit Frobenius-expansion proof supplied by Q23 since the cited Bourbaki proof is not in the literature.

proof.text:
Suppose $u:k\to A$ is any other field homomorphism with the stated residue composite and prescribed values. For fixed $n$, apply $u$ to the unique expansion from Step 1:
$$u(x)=\sum_e u(a_{n,e}(x))^{q_n}\beta^e.$$
Each $u(a_{n,e}(x))$ is a residue lift of $a_{n,e}(x)$, so its $q_n$th power is the coefficient defining $s_n(x)$ in Step 2. Hence $u(x)\equiv s(x)\pmod{\mathfrak m^{q_n}}$ for every $n$. Since $q_n$ tends to infinity, $u(x)-s(x)$ belongs to every $\mathfrak m^N$, whose intersection is zero by [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Thus $u=s$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q23-f4b8d63ac (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read ILO IV 2.1.1–2.1.4 (pdf pp.56–57, printed p.50). The item states the same thing as IV 2.1.4: a unique coefficient section of a complete Noetherian local ring of characteristic p sending a residue p-basis to arbitrarily chosen lifts. The added 'p prime' is justified: with Z/4, k=F_2=k^4 and the empty family, the statement fails, and ILO takes p prime throughout. The only citer, lem-per-coefficient-field-generic-differential-basis (Steps 1 and 6), works in a reduced local ring, where the characteristic is forced to be prime. Dropping lem-weil-pbc-p-basis-exists from stmt_deps is correct because the p-basis is assumed and defined inline. I re-derived all six steps. Step 1 is the base-p digit induction with uniqueness. Step 2 shows t_n is well defined because (a+μ)^{q_n}=a^{q_n}+μ^{q_n} with μ^{q_n} in m^{q_n}. Step 3 shows s_n is a ring map through the carry calculation. Step 4 shows the s_n are compatible for arbitrary lifts. Step 5 takes the limit through the completeness bijection. Step 6 proves uniqueness from the expansion plus ∩m^N=0. Steps cite only def-weil-ring-frobenius and def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring, whose statements cover what the steps take. Small cases checked: E=∅, A=k, F_p(u)[[t]], F_p(u)[ε]/ε². The DAG has no duplicate (searched coefficient-field, p-basis and Cohen nodes). The delivery has no new nodes, no route issue and no tool_uses; this review made no fixes.
